fields.sections.0.h: Alpha Launch Announcement and Browser Identity
fields.sections.1.h: Alpha Stage Limitations and User Participation Request
fields.sections.2.h: Security Vulnerability Disclosure and Security Researcher Welcome
fields.sections.3.h: Automatic Update System and Fast Improvement Cycle
fields.sections.4.h: Test Environment Provided for Web Developers
fields.sections.0.ko: The Ladybird development team officially announced entry into alpha stage on November 23, with immediate availability for macOS and Linux users. The core feature of this browser is that it is equipped with its own rendering engine built from scratch independently, rather than a fork based on existing WebKit or Chromium. The surrounding UI and features are simplified but at a usable level.
fields.sections.1.ko: As an alpha version, not all websites may function normally and intermittent crashes are expected. The development team transparently discloses this and invites users to report broken websites directly within the browser. When a crash occurs, users can review the crash report and choose whether to submit it, ensuring transparency through privacy policy.
fields.sections.2.ko: The development team acknowledges that new browsers being repeatedly hacked is an essential stage of development, and explicitly states it cannot guarantee security at this stage. Instead, it requests security experts to report vulnerabilities when found, demonstrating its commitment to progressively strengthen Ladybird through such feedback.
fields.sections.3.ko: Plans to operate an alpha channel continuously to distribute regular automatic updates, which is the part the development team finds most exciting. While Ladybird has been improving rapidly, users had to build source code directly to experience the latest version until now, but now general users can directly experience development progress.
fields.sections.4.ko: Website creators are encouraged to test their sites on Ladybird and report compatibility issues. To this end, it provides automated testing environments by supporting WebDriver standards and Firefox DevTools Protocol, thereby raising developer accessibility.
fields.sections.5.ko: The development team expresses gratitude to the entire community that has sponsored, reported bugs, and written code over a long period. While there is still much work to be done, the team expresses great satisfaction that users can now directly experience Ladybird.
fields.caveat: Since the current stage is an alpha version, meaningful conclusions on stability and compatibility assessment can only be drawn at subsequent beta and official release stages, and the author's claims reflect the development team's intent rather than objective performance verification.
